title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years for rape and sexual assault offences – latest updates
description:
Disgraced comedian must serve two-thirds of the 10 years and six month sentence before he will be eligible for parole

  • Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison

Proceedings are beginning now. Chief prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC is up on her feet. She’ll be the first to deliver remarks.

The sentencing has been pushed back as court staff attempt to rearrange the courtroom so one of the victims can be protected, PA reports.

Continue reading...
text: Brand sentenced to 10 years and six months for rape and sexual assault offences
Judge Bennathan asks Brand to stand up as he passes his sentence judgment.
He says the sentence for rape is nine years imprisonment.
The total sentence is 10 years, six months, with the sexual assault offences.
The judge gave prison sentences of nine months, 18 months, and eight months for those three offences.
Prosecutors had called for the judge to mete out a sentence of this severity, for a category one penalty which ranges from 10-15 years.

Judge Bennathan also commended the Met Police for “their hard work in gathering evidence and taking great care of all the women who testified.”
As I reported earlier, one of the victims said she had wanted to withdraw her case after the stress and pressure and public attention, but she persisted with the support of specialist police teams.
The Met Police have said they expect other women may come forward to report their experiences of abuse and assault.
Judge paid tribute to 'determination and bravery' of women who came forward
Right before delivering his sentence decision, Judge Bennathan said:

double quotation markFinally, before passing sentence, I pause to pay tribute to the determination and bravery of all the woman whose evidence I have been recounting. I do not increase your punishment becauseof it but all those women had to face being confronted and being told they lied, or twisted the truth, and or they’d agreed to your sexual demands. That was all done because of you, and your instructions.
Officers have taken Brand out of the courtroom.
He has served a few days at HMP Wandsworth already, after being denied bail last Thursday following his conviction.
Brand must serve two-thirds of the 10-and-a-half years sentence before he will be eligible for parole, says the judge.
That means he will be behind bars for seven years.
The judge says with the mitigating factors in play, he will reduce his sentence for Brand by a year.
He has not given the full sentence yet.
Judge Bennathan has repeatedly called Brand a sexual predator during his address so far.
He notes mitigating factors of no crimes having been reported in the past 17 years, and some evidence testifying to Brand’s character.
'You thought fame meant you could act however you liked'
The judge, laying out the crimes, notes Brand’s “staggering arrogance” and how his entourage regularly indulged Brand’s actions.

Three of the four crimes took place in public settings, in front of other people – at a bar, radio station and a setting where an advert was being filmed. Others in the room laughed after the assaults, the women said.
double quotation markThese insults in front of an audience, said after the assault amount to an additional humiliation.

double quotation markThe whole episode reeks of casual disrespect, and your belief that fame meant you could act however you liked, when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live.
The judge is relaying the sexual assaults Brand committed against the women.
He starts with the attacks on one woman in a pub in London where Brand groped the breast of a fellow party attendee.
“The effect on her had her wandering the streets of London, phoning a friend in the middle of the night, tearful and distressed.”
He outlines another assault, where Brand, visiting a radio station with an entourage launched himself at a woman, groping and kissing her in front of her colleagues and his entourage.
He notes the attack’s impact on her, how it damaged relationships with her male colleagues.
“There was the added humiliation of you assaulting her in front of an audience and the laughter afterwards”.
Judge Bennathan starts with Brand’s climb to fame 20 years ago.
“About 20 years ago, Russell Brand, you were becoming famous. You were clever – and in many people’s eyes, funny and charismatic.
“You had also become a sexual predator,” he says.
“Your status protected you until 2023 when journalists published allegations” about his rapes and sexual abuse of women.
Such public reporting “empowered” other women to come forward to police, says Bennathan.
Judge Bennathan is about to begin his sentencing remarks, having considered the submissions from the prosecutor and Brand’s defence lawyer this morning.
A reminder that Russell Brand, once one of Britain’s most high-profile actor-comedians, was convicted last Thursday of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others.

A jury of eight men and four women found him guilty of attacking four of six women on allegations dating back to 2004. He was cleared of two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault.
